sec: Acute hepatitis B: transmission, post-transfusion hepatitis, symptoms, investigations, marker curve, interpretation

items.q: Mode of transmission tree for acute hepatitis B — which is NOT one of the four printed arms?
items.exp: Arms: Vertical, Percutaneous, Sexual, Blood transfusion. 'No feco-oral / breast milk transmission.' (Book p1037)

items.q: Percutaneous risk figures printed for HBV and HCV?
Judge: I Sexual transmission risk is printed as 'not established'. II Blood-transfusion risk is 1 : 200,000 units and 1 : 1,800,000 with HBV > HBC (HCV).
items.exp: 'Sexual : Not established'; 'Blood Transfusion : 1 : 200000 units; 1 : 1800000 [HBV > HBC]'. (Book p1037)

items.q: Post-transfusion hepatitis — which hierarchy of agents is printed?
items.exp: 'Post Transfusion Hepatitis : Hepatitis following transfusion • CMV > EBV > HCV.' (Book p1037)

items.q: Symptoms of acute hepatitis B: duration of prodrome and when it appears?
opts: 2–3 days of prodromal phase after 60 days of IP
2–3 weeks of prodrome after 30 days IP
7 days of prodrome after 40 days IP
No prodrome; abrupt jaundice at 60 days
items.exp: '2–3 days of prodromal phase after 60 days of IP. Jaundice + ↑↑ enzymes (ALT/AST).' (Book p1037)

items.q: Investigations — match — 1) Anti-HAV IgM 2) Anti-HEV IgM … A) m/c cause in adults B) m/c cause in children
items.exp: 'Anti-HAV IgM (m/c cause : children). Anti-HEV IgM (m/c cause : adults). if both −ve → HBsAg, HBeAg, anti-HBc IgM.' (Book p1037)

items.q: HBV marker curve — match — 1) dark blue 2) red 3) green 4) purple … A) Anti-HBs B) HBsAg C) Total anti-HBc D) IgM anti-HBc
items.exp: Legend: HBsAg (blue), IgM Anti-HBc (red), Total Anti-HBc (green), Anti-HBs (purple). (Book p1037)

items.q: On the 'HBV infection markers' graph, the boxed window period sits between which weeks after exposure?
items.exp: The 'Window period' box lies over the 24–32-week span, after HBsAg falls and before anti-HBs rises; upper bands show HBeAg then Anti-HBe. (Book p1037)

items.q: Interpretation table — match — 1) HBsAg +, HBeAg +, anti-HBc IgM + 2) HBsAg +, HBeAg −, anti-HBc IgM + … A) Low infectivity & replication / pre-core gene mutant (unable to express HBeAg) B) Acute hepatitis with ↑ infectivity & replication
items.exp: Column 1 (all +): acute hepatitis with ↑ infectivity & replication. Column 2 (HBeAg −): low infectivity & replication / Pre core gene mutant unable to express HBeAg. (Book p1037)

items.q: Fill up (right-hand bullets): S gene / A gene / Escape / Occult gene mutation → ↓ viral load, won't express ______; best test: ______.
items.exp: 'Sgene/A gene/Escape/Occult gene mutation : ↓ viral load – Won't express HBsAg. Best test : Anti HBc IgM.' (Book p1037)

items.q: Basal core mutant expresses what percentage of HBeAg, per the bullet?
items.exp: 'Basal core mutant : Express 30% of HBeAg.' (Book p1037)

items.q: What is printed as the best marker for acute hepatitis at the bottom of the page?
items.exp: 'Best marker for acute hepatitis : HBV DNA load (Quantitative marker).' (Anti-HBc IgM is the best test for escape/occult mutants.) (Book p1037)
